fair_value.method: Horizon-date (Sep-2027) value on forward (2028-type) cash flows at a $5.85/lb realized copper deck and $4,000/oz gold: EV/EBITDA ~$689M x 6.0x less ~$150M net debt = $37.6 (45%), P/E $3.60 x 10.5x = $37.8 (35%), and a rebuilt long-life NAV at $5.00/lb long-term copper of ~$26 at 1.0x (20%); blend ~$35.4, rounded to $35.5. A $6.00 deck adds ~$1.2/share, a $5.50 deck removes ~$3.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Forward EBITDA as the market will see it in Sep-2027: 82kt Cu (haircut to the low half of the filed 80-90kt 2028 outlook for Ero's guidance-miss record) = 180.8 Mlb x 96% payable x ($5.85 realized - $2.25 C1) = ~$625M; Xavantina 55koz x ($4,000 - $1,300 AISC-type cost) = ~$149M; less ~$85M G&A/exploration/other = ~$689M. 6.0x = $4.13B EV, less ~$150M horizon net debt (Q2-26 $452.7M, peak capex in 2026, 2027 FCF ~$300M at ~$6 Cu), / 106M diluted shares (Q2-26 105.88M). Sensitivity: $6.00 deck -> ~$39.1; $5.50 deck -> ~$34.1.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Built (not consensus) forward EPS: EBITDA $689M - D&A ~$175M (2026 run-rate ~$151M from H1 $75.4M, rising with volume) - interest ~$30M = $484M pre-tax x (1 - 22% tax) = ~$377M / 106M = $3.56, call $3.60, x 10.5x (discount to larger copper peers for single-country Brazil, BRL and one-shaft execution risk, but credit for volume growth and deleveraging). Consensus 2027E $4.79 embeds a higher Cu/Au deck and is not used directly.

methods.name: other (P/NAV)
methods.inputs: Rebuilt from a simple life-of-operations cash-flow build (replaces round-1's unsourced ~$45 NAV): long-term $5.00/lb Cu and $3,200/oz Au from 2029; ~82kt Cu at C1 $2.25 and 55koz Au -> ~$495M EBITDA, less ~$130M sustaining capex and ~$75M cash tax = ~$290M/yr FCF over ~15 years at 8% (annuity 8.56) = ~$2.5B, plus ~$0.1B PV of 2028 above-deck cash flow, plus Furnas risked at ~$0.4B (60% attributable of the $2.0B 100%-basis PEA NPV8, then risked for PEA stage and Vale carry), less ~$0.15B horizon net debt = ~$2.75B / 106M = ~$26. Multiple 1.0x (peers ~0.82-0.95x on $4.00-4.50 decks; my deck is higher).

bear.story: Copper retreats from record LME ~$6.5/lb toward Citi-type ~$5.00-5.40 as China demand softens and US tariff stockpiling unwinds; Pilar shaft transition to operations slips into 2028, 2027 guidance (Feb-2027) set at the low end of 75-85kt with C1 above $2.35 on a strong post-election BRL once the collars' cap is breached; stock re-rates to ~4.5x ~$560M EBITDA.

base.story: LME copper averages ~$6.0-6.3/lb in 2027 (between Citi and Goldman's raised $13,800/t), Ero realizes ~$5.85; 2027 lands in 75-85kt with Pilar operational during the year and 2028 guided at 80-90kt; net debt falls to ~$100-200M by the horizon and a modest capital-return framework appears; stock trades ~6x forward EBITDA / ~10.5x EPS.

bull.story: Copper holds $6.50-7.00/lb in a structural deficit; Pilar and Tucuma filtration deliver the top half of guidance, forward EBITDA $900M+, net cash by mid/late 2027 with buybacks/dividend, and a positive Furnas PFS; re-rating to ~6.5x EV/EBITDA.

thesis_break_reason: At $23 the equity is ~$2.44B and EV ~$2.6-2.75B (net debt ~$150-300M depending on the path): ~3.9x my base forward EBITDA (~$690M) and still only ~4.9x a $5.00/lb-copper 2027 EBITDA (~$550M at ~78kt, C1 $2.28, 55koz Au plus the last historic gold concentrate). Getting there needs copper sustained below ~$5/lb, under every current bank 2027 forecast (Citi ~$5.44, Goldman ~$6.26), or a company-specific failure (Pilar shaft not operational in 2027, Tucuma filtration not lifting throughput, 2027 guidance well below 75-85kt). Note: I compute ~4.9x rather than the supervisor's ~3.8x at $5.00 copper, but the conclusion is the same.

Use of FCF: debt repayment vs. capital returns vs. Furnas funding
reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor fact-checked several of my round-1 inputs and I accept its evidenced findings: (1) my ~$45 NAV was unsourced and circular; peers trade ~0.82-0.95x NAV on conservative decks, so I rebuilt NAV from an explicit cash-flow build and get ~$26 at $5.00 long-term copper, which is the single largest change; (2) the BRL collars ($450M, floor 5.40, cap 6.34) run to Dec-2027, which I verified in the Q2-26 MD&A, so 2027 costs are partly protected; (3) my $5.50 deck was at the bottom of bank 2027 views (Goldman raised to $13,800/t, verified; Citi ~$12,000/t), and Ero realized $5.78 in Q2 with LME lower than today, so I move to $5.85 realized, slightly below the supervisor's $6.00 because realized runs a few percent under LME and spot is at a record; (4) no guidance change was filed at the Sept CMD, so the filed 75-85kt (2027) / 80-90kt (2028) outlook stands; I still haircut to 82kt for execution risk; (5) consensus 2027E EPS $4.79 embeds a richer deck, so I replaced it with a built EPS of ~$3.60 (D&A ~$175M, interest ~$30M, 22% tax; H1-26 D&A $75.4M verified) at 10.5x. I also updated gold to ~$4,000 (spot ~$4,280 on 9/25, vs my round-1 $3,800). Net: cash-flow methods sit at ~$37.6-37.8, NAV at ~$26, blend ~$35.5, down from $38.6 almost entirely because of the NAV rebuild; the deck and hedge corrections roughly offset the lower built EPS. For the distribution I keep a lognormal (median $37, sigma 0.46, below the 64% realized vol that was inflated by a one-way copper rally but far above the 25-35% large-cap base rate) mixed 85/15 with a fatter bear component (median $30, sigma 0.65) for a copper reversal from records. That gives a median of ~$36 and a mean of ~$40. The faster deleveraging and hedge findings nudge the center up about $0.5 versus round 1, while the lower fair value keeps it below spot, so P(>= $38) is ~0.46 (was 0.445) and P(>= $23) ~0.82 (was 0.80). Where I differ from the supervisor: its thesis-break math (~3.8x at $5.00 Cu) looks low; I compute ~4.9x, which does not change the $23 level. Research: 4 extra searches/fetches (Q2-26 MD&A and release on EDGAR, Goldman forecast, gold spot, Pilar timing); no option data or priors used.
